title: Custom Carbon Rim Hole Patterns & Drilling Angles
intro: We normally model the hub drawing, rim dimensions and lacing to customize hole positions and angles that follow the spoke directions.
openVideo: Play automated angled rim drilling video
videoCaption: Automated angled drilling · Watch the machining process

axialCapability.label: Left/right offset holes and axial angles
axialCapability.description: We support left/right offset rim holes, matching each axial drilling angle to the hole position and corresponding hub flange offset.

longitudinalCapability.label: Longitudinal angles for the lacing
longitudinalCapability.description: Set the two longitudinal drilling angles to match flange PCD, hole count and the lacing pattern.

alignmentPrinciple.title: Designed to avoid forced bends
alignmentPrinciple.description: Match two axial and two longitudinal angles together to reduce forced bending at the nipple exit and bring tension transfer closer to coaxial alignment.
alignmentPrinciple.manufacturingLimit: Avoiding forced bends is a design goal, not a guarantee of exact coaxial alignment in the finished wheel.

staticDrillingIllustrations.title: Choose a lacing pattern to see drilling directions
staticDrillingIllustrations.introduction: Read the lacing and crossing count on one flange, then compare the local details to understand drilling directions.
staticDrillingIllustrations.additionalSupportedPatterns: These three common lacing patterns are examples. We also support 2:1, G3 and other layouts. Use the “{simulatorButtonLabel}” button to explore more patterns.
staticDrillingIllustrations.selectionLabel: Choose a lacing pattern for the static drilling illustrations
staticDrillingIllustrations.drillingAxisLegend: Local details · Dashed: matched hole axis
staticDrillingIllustrations.longitudinalViewDescription: Green and blue show one seat from each flange, with each hole axis following its spoke through the rim wall.
staticDrillingIllustrations.axialViewDescription: We support left/right offset rim holes (L / R) with axial angles matched to the flanges. WL / WR measure each flange's distance from the hub center plane.
staticDrillingIllustrations.axialImageAlt: Axial projection of left/right offset rim holes. L and R identify holes on either side of the rim centerline, with each hole axis pointing toward its hub flange. WL and WR show the flange offsets.
staticDrillingIllustrations.drawingLimit: These illustrations show direction relationships only. Actual hole angles require drawing and dimension modeling. The topology simulator displays lacing; it does not output machining angles.

radial.label: Radial lacing
radial.crossingGuide: The green reference spoke runs radially to the rim without crossing another spoke on the same flange.
radial.description: In the front projection, spokes run radially between flange and rim. Longitudinal hole axes follow them, while axial alignment still depends on both flange positions.
radial.wheelImageAlt: One-flange view of a 32-hole radially laced wheel, showing all 16 spokes on that flange. The green reference spoke has no same-flange crossings.
radial.longitudinalImageAlt: Separate local details of two radial-lacing seats, with longitudinal hole axes following radial spokes through the rim wall.

twoCross.label: Two-cross lacing
twoCross.crossingGuide: Follow the green reference spoke from hub to rim: 1 and 2 mark crossings with spokes on the same flange.
twoCross.description: Two-cross means each spoke crosses two other spokes attached to the same flange. Its approach to the rim tilts away from the local radius, so the longitudinal hole axis must follow the spoke.
twoCross.wheelImageAlt: One-flange view of a 32-hole two-cross wheel, showing all 16 spokes on that flange. Crossings 1 and 2 are marked along the green reference spoke from hub to rim.
twoCross.longitudinalImageAlt: Separate local details of two two-cross seats, with each hole axis following its spoke's tilt through the rim wall.

threeCross.label: Three-cross lacing
threeCross.crossingGuide: Follow the green reference spoke from hub to rim: 1, 2 and 3 mark crossings with spokes on the same flange.
threeCross.description: Three-cross means each spoke crosses three other spokes attached to the same flange. Its approach to the rim differs from two-cross lacing, so the longitudinal drilling angles must be matched again.
threeCross.wheelImageAlt: One-flange view of a 32-hole three-cross wheel, showing all 16 spokes on that flange. Crossings 1, 2 and 3 are marked along the green reference spoke from hub to rim.
threeCross.longitudinalImageAlt: Separate local details of two three-cross seats, with longitudinal hole axes adjusted to the spoke approach directions.

hubDrawingGeometry.title: Simulate geometry from the hub drawing
hubDrawingGeometry.description: We normally use drawing dimensions for WL / WR, left/right flange PCD and spoke exits, together with rim ERD, hole positions and lacing, to model spoke directions in space.

matchedDrillingAngles.title: Match four drilling angles
matchedDrillingAngles.description: Convert the modeled spoke directions into hole positions and axes. Drawing revision, hole layout and the machining plan are confirmed directly.

manufacturingAndAssemblyTolerances.title: Account for manufacturing and assembly tolerances
manufacturingAndAssemblyTolerances.description: Drawing dimensions have tolerances, and actual hubs, rim molding, drilling and assembly also vary. Nominal dimensions in the simulation cannot be treated as identical to the finished fit.

carbonRimInterior.title: Limits of the molded carbon rim interior
carbonRimInterior.description: The internal nipple seats of a closed carbon rim are formed during molding and cannot be trued by CNC turning around the full internal circumference. Even a smooth interior has local surface variation that affects nipple contact. Custom drilling can closely match the drawing geometry, but cannot also remove interior variation or assembly deviations.

angleAlignmentBenefits.title: Reduce fatigue risks at three load-critical points
angleAlignmentBenefits.misalignmentExplanation: When fixed drilling angles do not match the actual hub and lacing, tension can force the nipple to tilt and the spoke to bend at its thread transition. This extra bending and side loading can contribute to nipple-seat cracking and spoke fatigue failure.

spokeEndFatigue.mechanism: Less forced bending and extra bending moment
spokeEndFatigue.title: Lower spoke thread-root failure risk
spokeEndFatigue.description: Reduce additional bending stress at the spoke thread transition, lowering the risk of local fatigue and breakage under repeated loads.

nippleSideLoading.title: Less nipple side loading and damage
nippleSideLoading.description: Let the nipple follow the spoke's load direction more freely, reducing tilt, one-sided loading and local deformation.

rimHoleLocalDamage.mechanism: Less seat side loading and stress concentration
rimHoleLocalDamage.title: Lower carbon rim nipple-seat cracking risk
rimHoleLocalDamage.description: Reduce lateral nipple pressure against the hole wall and seat edge, limiting local stress concentrations and fatigue damage.

angleAlignmentBenefits.assemblyContext: Angle matching works together with suitable nipples, washers where specified by the design, and correct wheel-building tension.

holeLayout.label: Hole layouts and left/right offsets
holeLayout.description: Left/right offset holes, standard and special arrangements are supported. Hole offsets and axial angles are confirmed from the drawings and wheel design.

oemOdm.label: OEM / ODM
oemOdm.description: Custom compatibility with hub and lacing designs.

customization.title: Details needed for custom drilling
customization.intro: Prepare these details so we can confirm the drilling plan directly:

items.hubDrawingAndRevision: Hub drawing and revision, including WL / WR, flange PCDs and spoke exits
items.rimDimensionsAndHoleCount: Rim model, ERD, hole count and left/right hole offset requirements
items.lacingAndNippleAssembly: Intended lacing, nipples and washer arrangement

commitment.title: Automated machining and consistency
commitment.body: Our self-developed automated machinery controls consistency in hole placement and axis direction, enabling repeatable production of custom drilling patterns.

seo.title: Custom Carbon Rim Drilling: Hub Drawings & Lacing Angles
seo.description: Custom carbon rim drilling matched to hub drawings and lacing. Supports left/right offset holes, two-cross, three-cross, 2:1 and G3 layouts, with real wheel photos.
seo.imageAlt: Automated equipment drilling a carbon rim spoke hole at a specified angle
seo.videoName: Automated angled spoke-hole drilling for carbon rims
seo.videoDescription: Factory footage of automated equipment drilling a carbon rim spoke hole along a specified direction. Hole positions and angles are confirmed from hub drawings, rim dimensions and spoke lacing.

consultation.title: Confirm drilling for your hub and lacing
consultation.description: Prepare your hub drawing, rim model, hole count and intended lacing. Contact us to review matching geometry and machining requirements.
